summary: This is an event class that wraps an Employee object and provides a fluent interface to modify the employee's properties. It uses Laravel's Dispatchable trait, which allows the event to be triggered and broadcast throughout the application. The methods each update a single employee property and return the event object itself, enabling you to chain multiple method calls together.

explanations.3: The namespace declaration tells PHP where this class lives in the file structure — think of it as the 'address' of the class so other parts of the app can import it.
explanations.10: The 'use Dispatchable' trait gives this event class special powers from Laravel, including the ability to be sent out as an event that listeners can respond to.
explanations.12: The constructor accepts an Employee object and stores it as a private property using PHP 8's constructor property promotion — this is shorthand for declaring and assigning in one line.
explanations.16: These methods (setFirstName, setLastName, setPseudo) return `$this`, which means the method returns the entire event object itself — this enables method chaining so you can call multiple setters in a row like `$event->setFirstName('John')->setLastName('Doe')->setPseudo('JD')`.
